clue.text: Posturing when playing records?

definitions.meaning: behaving affectedly, giving oneself false grandeur
airs are tunes, so playing records means putting tunes on

explanation.definitionFit: Posturing is the idiom for acting superior; spinning discs literally sets tunes going, the playful second sense.

clue.text: Regular habit

definitions.meaning: a habit is a distinctive costume, as a monk's

explanation.definitionFit: Something regular is consistent in form; a habit is a prescribed outfit, as worn by a nun or soldier.

clue.text: Diet could well be restricted

indicators.note: says the letters of the word diet might well form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A slimmer's eating plan may be limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could well be' rearranges DIET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied means bound or constrained, a synonym of restricted.

clue.text: Essential for the minute writer?

parts.note: minute suggests something tiny, but here it means the minutes of a meeting, which a secretary jots down on paper

explanation.surface: What a person writing very small needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper is what a minute-taker writes the record of a meeting on.

clue.text: The alternative to a sound discoursing

parts.note: or is the word introducing an alternative
a ting is a light ringing sound

explanation.surface: Choosing between options in a sound way while holding forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Discoursing is speaking at length, as an orator does in a formal speech.

clue.text: Some oaf, arrogant when abroad

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boorish fellow is particularly haughty on holiday overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far away, in a distant land, is what abroad suggests; the adverb means at a distance.

clue.text: Figure out a way to get cash for property

definitions.meaning: to convert assets into money by selling them

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to grasp a fact and to turn holdings into money, as in realising an investment.

clue.text: Operating levers closing gates by railway track

indicators.note: working the levers puts their letters, along with closing, into a new order

explanation.surface: A signalman pulls levers that shut the gates beside the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating' rearranges LEVERS and CLOSING together; the surface paints a signal box, so the anagram is well hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A road crossing a railway on the same level is guarded by gates that close when trains pass.

clue.text: Appearing simultaneously nevertheless

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both coinciding in time and, as a conjunction-like adverb, however.

clue.text: At one time one fellow would be pressing

parts.note: ex means former, once
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: In the past a single man would be urgent.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means urgent or demanding immediate attention.

clue.text: A mad arrangement the worker finds very hard

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of a mad puts them in a different order

parts.note: the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A crazy scheme that an employee finds difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant originally named a legendary unbreakable stone, hence unyielding.

clue.text: Famous statue seen in these rose-gardens

indicators.note: seen in says the answer appears inside the following words

explanation.surface: A celebrated sculpture on view in these flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'these' and 'rose'. The statue is the figure atop the fountain in London's Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The aluminium figure in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly called by the Greek love god's name.

clue.text: Spring in the country

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Springtime out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a nation of south-west Europe.

clue.text: Soldiers return to hospital sound that's sad

indicators.note: the soldiers come back, so their word is read in reverse

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Troops come back to a ward with a mournful noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigh is a long breath expressing sorrow.

clue.text: Setting a scholar against a philosopher

parts.note: a BA is a holder of a Bachelor of Arts degree
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Placing a learned person in opposition to a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon was the English philosopher of empirical method.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon, the Elizabethan essayist and statesman, is a famous English thinker.

clue.text: Directors get on

definitions.meaning: the governing body of a company
to embark on a ship, train or plane

explanation.definitionFit: A company's governing panel shares the name with the verb for boarding a vehicle.

clue.text: Given business award in addition to order

parts.note: Co. is short for company
MM is the Military Medal, a British award
and means in addition

explanation.surface: Granted a company prize as well as a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is an instruction or order.

clue.text: They always have work on hand

definitions.text: They always have work on hand

parts.words: They always have work on hand
parts.note: on hand sounds like having plenty to do, but literally these makers produce what goes over a hand

explanation.surface: Busy people who are never short of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Makers of hand coverings are always working on things worn on a hand.

clue.text: Doctor beset by eccentric stout in the extreme

indicators.note: the doctor is surrounded on both sides by the other letters
an eccentric arrangement of stout scrambles its letters

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A physician surrounded by a strange stout fellow at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns STOUT into OUTST; 'beset by' places MO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outmost means farthest out, at the extreme edge.

clue.text: Reached high to marry, taking in royalty

indicators.note: the word for marry takes in the royal letters

parts.note: to wed is to marry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Climbed up in order to wed a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that towered rose to a great height.

clue.text: Try to contain Oriental politician's violent outburst

indicators.note: the word for try holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to test is to try out
E stands for eastern
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Attempt to hold back an Eastern MP's furious tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a storm, and figuratively an uproar or emotional eruption.

clue.text: Measure gun on an old ship

parts.note: a yard is a unit of length
a gun is a firearm, an arm

explanation.surface: A gauge for firearms aboard a vintage vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the end of a spar on a square-rigged sailing ship's mast.

clue.text: Americans look for a denial on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror runs backwards, so both pieces together are turned around

parts.note: to seek is to look for
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: US citizens search for a refusal when thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns SEEKNAY round as a whole to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is a colloquial name for people from the United States.

clue.text: Leave a group instrumentalists performing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: Musicians in a group playing a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or leave behind.

clue.text: Scatters pigs

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means strewing seed; the noun names adult female swine.

clue.text: Polish people featured in a newspaper leader

indicators.note: the people appear within the editor's letters

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper
men means people

explanation.surface: Poles appearing in a newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb meaning refine.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and refine it.

clue.text: Endure final

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to keep going over time; the adjective means at the end.

clue.text: Pace about head

indicators.note: about means around, the letters of pace being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Walk around the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges PACE. A head is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a promontory, as is a cape.

clue.text: The rising market for a particular vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A booming market for one type of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger car running on street rails.

clue.text: Hurried back to put in class report

indicators.note: back says the word for hurried is written backwards

parts.note: ran means hurried
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Rushed back to enrol in a class presentation.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or give an account.

clue.text: Find me a lord and his estate

indicators.note: find here asks the solver to discover a new word within the letters of me a lord

explanation.surface: Seek out a nobleman and his lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' rearranges ME A LORD. 'his' refers back to the lord.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the territory or rank held by a peer of that title.

clue.text: "Promise, large promise, is the soul of an" (Samuel Johnston)

definitions.text: "Promise, large promise, is the soul of an" (Samuel Johnston)

parts.words: "Promise, large promise, is the soul of an" (Samuel Johnston)
parts.note: a fill-in from Johnson's Idler essay about commercial notices that promise much

explanation.surface: A quotation from the great lexicographer awaiting its final word.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson wrote this in The Idler, 1759; the paper prints his name as Johnston.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting products by bold claims is the essence of a commercial notice.
